Role :- Senior Product Manager (Revenue)
Experience :- 5+ Years

About Fam (previously FamPay)

Fam is India’s first payments app for everyone above 11. FamApp helps make online and offline payments through UPI and FamCard. We are on a mission to raise a new, financially aware generation, and drive 250 million+ young users in India to kickstart their financial journey super early in their life.

We’re reimagining how the next generation experiences fintech—going beyond payments to build a lifestyle brand that blends money, identity, and everyday experiences into one seamless, intuitive journey.
Founded in 2019 by IIT Roorkee alumni, Fam is backed by some of the most respected investors around the world like Elevation Capital, Y-Combinator, Peak XV (Sequoia Capital) India, Venture Highway, Global Founder’s Capital and the likes of Kunal Shah, Amrish Rao as angel investors.

Roles & Responsibilities :-

Drive product vision and execution: Translate the broader product strategy into actionable roadmaps and deliver measurable impact
Own key funnels or metrics – define, monitor, and improve critical KPIs such as activation, retention, CSAT, or revenue
Collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Design, Growth, and Analytics teams to deliver end-to-end solutions
Identify and solve real user problems by deeply understanding user needs, identifying opportunities, validating hypotheses, and delivering delightful experiences
Be data-informed: Use quantitative and qualitative data to prioritize features and evaluate success post-launch
Ensure high-quality product documentation by writing clear, structured PRDs and contributing to improved product processes
Mentor and guide PMs through structured feedback, sharing best practices, and conducting product reviews
Influence through user advocacy: Balance business goals with user empathy and data-driven decision-making
Collaborate with teams to align on product priorities, share insights, and communicate progress effectively
Get hands dirty when needed: Participate in discovery, design reviews, QA, or data deep-dives as required

Must Haves :

5–8 years of experience in Product Management, ideally in B2C or consumer-facing products
Proven track record of owning a key product metric (e.g., acquisition, activation, retention, revenue, NPS, CSAT, etc) and driving it end-to-end
Experience working closely with Design and Engineering teams to conceptualise, prioritise, and ship impactful features
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills – ability to translate data into insights and insights into product decisions
Hands-on experience with funnel analysis and experimentation (A/B testing)
Past experience in writing and reviewing PRDs and driving execution from idea to launch
Excellent communication and documentation skills with clarity, depth, and stakeholder alignment
Strong consumer understanding – ability to empathize with users and identify what drives delight vs. friction
Executional ownership – solving real problems and delivering measurable business outcomes
Actively leverages AI in day-to-day workflows and is familiar with tools beyond just GPT/Claude

Good to Have :-

Experience in FinTech, Payments, or B2C commerce
Exposure to ads, revenue, or customer retention initiatives
Prior experience as an engineer turned PM or strong technical understanding of frontend/backend systems
Comfort working in ambiguous, fast-paced environments
Exposure to KYC, Customer Support, Retention, and Growth verticals
Experience in building for scale, leveraging consumer insights and data to prioritize product bets
Understanding of design systems, usability principles, and user behavior analytics tools
Experience mentoring or managing small product pods or PMs
Proven ability to mentor junior PMs or cross-functional teams

This role is eligible for our hybrid work model: Two days in-office.

Senior Product Manager

Our Product Design and Management teams work tirelessly to understand what our customers need and make it a reality. They’re the ones who make our deals come to life and our user experience simple and intuitive.

Why This Job’s a Big Deal

As a Senior Product Manager in the Product Operating Model (POM), your focus is on defining, prioritizing, and delivering products or capabilities that solve customer problems and deliver measurable business outcomes. You are accountable for the success of your product, partnering closely with design, engineering, and business stakeholders. You balance customer needs, business goals, and technical feasibility to ensure your product creates real value.

In This Role You Will Get To

1. Product Discovery & Strategy

Understand the flight order lifecycle through research, data analysis, and feedback loops
Define the product vision, goals, and outcomes in alignment with the group and portfolio strategy to reduce risk to flights P&L. 
Research, troubleshoot, diagnose, and recommend solutions to complex business and technical problems.
Translate data insights and market trends into product opportunities
Outcome Ownership
Define, track, and deliver against product outcomes, lagging and leading indicators. Focused on outcomes over output. 
Balance short-term risks, long-term opportunities , technical debt, and enabler work in your product backlog.
Continuously evaluate whether product initiatives are driving intended value
Stakeholder Alignment & Communication
Collaborate with stakeholders across the organization, including Commercial Teams, Finance, Technology, Accounting, and Financial Planning & Analysis to bring products to market.
Partner with business sponsors, portfolio managers, and cross-functional teams to align on outcomes
Partner with Data teams to identify insights that drive faster decision making. 
Act as the voice of the flights business and advocate for value delivery in decision-making.
Planning & Execution
Lead quarterly and sprint planning for your product team with an outcomes focused approach. 
Ensure dependencies are identified, managed, and communicated
Participate in demos, standups, and retrospectives to support delivery progress.
Roll up your sleeves. We are a lean team and there is no job either big or too small. Some days you will be planning for the next quarter, and other days you will be diving into database records or inspecting API responses to help the development team troubleshoot an issue. We are very hands-on.

Who You Are

Requires a Bachelor's degree; an MBA is preferred.
6 to 8 years of experience taking full ownership of product success by defining visions and managing priorities to drive business and customer value.
A strategic thinker capable of connecting business opportunities with technical execution across engineering and design teams.
Strong quantitative skills with a focus on data-driven decision-making; knowledge of SQL, Tableau, and BigQuery is advantageous.
Active practitioner of the Product Operating Model, skilled at making trade-offs and empowering teams to deliver consistent value.
An effective communicator who builds alignment across teams and stakeholders fostering a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer-centricity within the Flights team and throughout the organization
Experienced at translating complex problems into clear product requirements and roadmaps with a strong understanding of technical architecture,
Highly organized, self-directed, and focused on outcomes over output
Illustrated history of living the values necessary to Priceline: Customer, Innovation, Team, Accountability and Trust
The Right Results, the Right Way is not just a motto at Priceline; it’s a way of life. Unquestionable integrity and ethics is essential.

Who We Are

WE ARE PRICELINE.

Our success as one of the biggest players in online travel is all thanks to our incredible, dedicated team of talented employees. Priceliners are focused on being the best travel deal makers in the world, motivated by our passion to help everyone experience the moments that matter most in their lives. Whether it’s a dream vacation, your cousin’s graduation, or your best friend’s wedding - we make travel affordable and accessible to our customers.

Our culture is unique and inspiring (that’s what our employees tell us). We’re a grown-up, startup. We deliver the excitement of a new venture, without the struggles and chaos that can come with a business that hasn’t stabilized.

We’re on the cutting edge of innovative technologies. We keep the customer at the center of all that we do. Our ability to meet their needs relies on the strength of a workforce as diverse as the customers we serve. We bring together employees from all walks of life and we are proud to provide the kind of inclusive environment that stimulates innovation, creativity and collaboration.

Priceline is part of the Booking Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: BKNG) family of companies, a highly profitable global online travel company with a market capitalization of over $80 billion. Our sister companies include Booking.com, BookingGo, Agoda, Kayak and OpenTable.

If you want to be part of something truly special, check us out!

Flexible work at Priceline

Priceline is following a hybrid working model, which includes two days onsite as determined by you and your manager (ideally selecting among Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday). On the remaining days, you can choose to be remote or in the office.

Perks & Benefits At Priceline

Our benefits are designed to support your health, wellbeing, and life inside and outside of work. Eligible Priceliners have access to:

Health & wellness coverage including medical, dental, vision, and mental health resources

Generous time off including PTO, holidays, a company-wide Priceline Pause reset week, and paid volunteer days

Work/life support including the ability to work up to 4 weeks per year from anywhere, parental leave, dependent care and family support resources, Summer Fridays, and office perks like stocked kitchens and catered meals (varies by location)

Financial security programs such as retirement plans with company contributions, life and disability coverage, and tax-advantaged accounts

Signature travel perks including employee-only discounts on hotels and flights, VIP deals, and Big Deal Bucks credits

Additional perks & discounts like travel and partner discounts, tuition support, legal support, and pet benefits

A people-first culture with Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), social events, recognition programs, and service awards that help you connect, grow, and celebrate together

Specific benefits and programs vary by location.

Inclusion is a Big Deal!

To be the best travel dealmakers in the world, we believe our team should reflect the broad range of customers and communities we serve. We are committed to cultivating a culture where all employees have the freedom to bring their individual perspectives, life experiences, and passion to work.

Priceline is a proud equal opportunity employer. We embrace and celebrate the unique lenses through which our employees see the world. We’d love for you to join us and help shape what makes our team extraordinary.

Applying for this position

We're excited that you are interested in a career with us. For all current employees, please use the internal portal to find jobs and apply.

External candidates are required to have an account before applying. When you click Apply, returning candidates can log in, or new candidates can quickly create an account to save/view applications.

Job Title: Product Manager — AI-native product builder
Experience: 3+ Years
Employment type: Full-time
Location: Chennai (exceptional global candidates may be considered)

Role Overview:
Codewalla is looking for a Product Manager who is becoming a product builder: someone who can move from a messy business problem to evidence, a working prototype, a product decision, shipped software, and a measurable outcome. This is not backlog administration or strategy in isolation; you are expected to get close to the product and help build it.

What we look for:
Meaningful end-to-end ownership of software products, with strong product sense across problem framing, prioritization, simplification, and trade-offs.
High agency, curiosity, humility, and strong judgment; willingness to change your mind when evidence changes.
A builder's instinct: comfort creating prototypes and using modern AI development tools to answer questions yourself.
Technical fluency to reason about APIs, data, architecture implications, reliability, model behavior, and constraints.
Evidence-based decision-making using customer research, analytics, operational data, experiments, and product economics.
Clear writing and communication with global clients and senior stakeholders.

What you will do
Find the sharp problem behind a request, workflow, or business ambition; make assumptions explicit and challenge the initial solution when evidence points elsewhere.
Move quickly from discussion to evidence through research, data analysis, interactive prototypes, technical spikes, synthetic scenarios, and small experiments.
Use AI coding and prototyping tools to explore product behavior yourself and improve collaboration with design and engineering.
Define measurable customer, operational, and business outcomes before significant engineering investment; shape the smallest responsible release and make trade-offs visible.
Reduce unnecessary PRDs, meetings, tickets, and handoffs—create only the artifacts that improve decisions and execution.
Stay involved through implementation, QA/UAT, launch, instrumentation, and post-launch learning; use evidence to decide what to change, continue, or stop.
Continuously improve how the team builds by experimenting with AI workflows and sharing what works.

Building AI products
Recognize where AI genuinely changes a workflow or outcome and where conventional software is the better answer.
Understand model capabilities and limitations well enough to design around what is possible; define evals, test cases, failure taxonomies, quality thresholds, human review, escalation, and feedback loops.
Treat trust, privacy, security, latency, cost, reliability, and hallucination risk as product constraints—and never confuse a compelling demo with a dependable product.
Measure AI-enabled work through outcomes such as productivity, cycle time, adoption, conversion, revenue, cost, quality, or risk.

About Codewalla:
Codewalla is a New York-based product and technology company with engineering teams in India. Since 2005, we have helped global clients build new software products, modernize existing platforms, and solve complex business and operational problems. Our teams work across enterprise platforms, SaaS products, mobile applications, workflow systems, platform modernization and AI-enabled product development. With our Chennai office, launched on November 2025, we are building a high-performance product and engineering teams that works closely with New York-based leadership and global clients. To know more about us visit: Enterprise Software Modernization & Digital Product Delivery | Codewalla

Why Join Codewalla?
Solve meaningful product challenges from discovery to launch.
Influence products before solutions are predefined.
Collaborate with experienced Product Managers, Engineers, and global leadership.
Build expertise in AI-native product development.
Competitive compensation, health benefits, professional development, and modern design tools.

Sr Product Manager, Financial Services
Location: Ahmedabad | Experience: 4+ years in Product Management

About the Role
Delhivery is building a platform to help transporters and fleet owners access financial and vehicle-related services through one platform. With FASTag, payments, wallet and GPS journeys already launched, the next phase includes expanding banking partnerships, automating payments, launching fuel service and building lending capabilities.
As Product Manager for Financial Services, you will own initiatives from discovery through launch and adoption. You will work closely with engineering, business, operations, finance, compliance and external partners to deliver reliable products that simplify customers’ daily operations.

What You Will Do
Own the roadmap and outcomes: Translate customer needs and business priorities into a focused roadmap across FASTag, wallets, Fuel Card, GPS and upcoming lending products. Track adoption, transaction success, revenue and servicing costs.
Understand customers and field operations: Spend time with transporters, fleet owners, sales and support teams. Identify friction across onboarding, KYC, purchase, fulfilment, activation and ongoing usage.
Build reliable transaction journeys: Improve recharges, refunds, reconciliation, disputes and invoicing. Anticipate failed transactions, partner downtime and exceptions, with clear recovery paths for customers and operations.
Expand the product portfolio: Drive new bank integrations, automated recharges, prepaid wallet integration and GPS offerings. Develop lending journeys spanning discounting, loan origination, servicing and co-lending partnerships.
Manage integrations and controls: Work with banks, payment providers and technology partners on API readiness, testing and production stability. Partner with compliance and finance on consent, data sharing, KYC and transaction controls.
Drive execution and practical automation: Write clear requirements, make prioritisation trade-offs and own rollout and post-launch improvements. Apply AI and workflow automation where they improve customer experience, accuracy or operating efficiency.

What You Bring
4+ years of product management experience, with demonstrated ownership from problem discovery through delivery and measurable outcomes.
Prior experience in fintech, payments or lending is preferred, not mandatory. Strong product fundamentals and the ability to learn complex domains matter.
Strong analytical skills and hands-on SQL proficiency to investigate funnels, transaction failures and customer behaviour.
Technical fluency to discuss APIs, integrations, data flows and system reliability with engineering and external partners.
Ability to work through ambiguity, understand operational details and balance customer experience, commercial goals and compliance requirements.
Practical familiarity with AI tools for research, prototyping, analysis and automation, with sound judgment about their limitations.
Clear communication and the ability to align stakeholders, resolve dependencies and drive adoption after launch.

Why This Role
Build on a live platform while shaping its next stage of growth. This role offers ownership across everyday transaction products and new lending capabilities, with direct impact on how transporters access services, manage payments and keep their businesses moving.

Who we are
Money. A subject that’s always on our mind. At Jupiter, our mission is to help people build a better relationship with money - simple, transparent, and empowering.
We’re a financial services platform that brings banking, lending, and investments together in one intuitive, tech-first experience. From savings and credit cards to instant personal loans and SIPs, everything we build is designed to help users manage and grow their money effortlessly.
Founded in 2019 by Jitendra Gupta (ex-Citrus Pay), Jupiter has grown to over 2.7 million users, backed by a strong portfolio of lending, rewards, and wealth products. With offerings like the Edge RuPay Credit Card, No-Penalty SIPs, and Daily SIPs, we continue to push boundaries in digital finance.

About the Role
We are looking for a Product Manager – Unsecured Lending to drive the evolution of Jupiter’s lending stack across personal loans, salary advances, and future credit constructs.
This role demands deep product ownership and execution depth from crafting a frictionless user journey to solving risk, compliance, and growth problems with product thinking. You’ll work closely with engineering, credit, data science, and risk teams to deliver scalable, compliant, and customer-obsessed lending experiences.

What You’ll Do
Own the end-to-end lending product lifecycle, from conceptualization, design, and build to launch and scale.
Deep-dive into data and funnels to identify friction points, improve conversions, and reduce drop-offs.
Build and enhance user journeys across loan origination, KYC, underwriting, disbursal, repayment, and collections.
Work cross-functionally with engineering, credit, compliance, and risk to deliver compliant and high-impact product outcomes.
Collaborate with risk and data teams to design smarter underwriting logic, improve approval rates, and maintain portfolio quality.
Stay compliant and audit-ready by ensuring alignment with RBI’s Digital Lending Guidelines and Fair Practices Code.
Define success metrics - activation rate, approval %, NPA %, ROA, funnel conversion, and improve them continuously.
Champion user empathy - build for real user credit needs, not just numbers.

What You’ll Bring
2–4 years of product management experience, preferably in fintech, digital lending, or credit products.
Strong grasp of the digital lending lifecycle, user acquisition, e-KYC, underwriting, disbursal, servicing, and collections.
Working experience on LMS and LOS is a must.
Familiarity with credit bureau APIs (CIBIL, Experian) and risk decision engines.
Data-driven mindset with proven ability to use analytics for decision-making.
Experience collaborating with engineering and design teams in fast-paced environments.
Understanding of RBI regulations, KFS requirements, and digital lending guidelines.
Strong problem-solving ability, ownership, and clarity of thought.

Why Jupiter
Work at the intersection of technology and finance, shaping the future of digital lending in India.
Ownership from day one you define, build, and scale the product.
Collaborate with industry-leading product, risk, and data teams.
A culture that rewards initiative, speed, and learning over hierarchy.

IT Product Manager | Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh

Location: Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh

Experience: 4–8 years

Role: IT Product Manager

Languages: Telugu and English

Travel: Regular travel across Andhra Pradesh

About The Role

We are looking for an IT Product Manager to lead the development of technology products and digital solutions for real-world challenges across Agriculture, Horticulture, Livestock and Fisheries in Andhra Pradesh.

This is a hands-on product role that combines product strategy, user discovery, technology, data and field implementation.

You will work closely with government departments, field teams, users and technology teams to understand problems, define product opportunities and take solutions from discovery and product definition through development, pilot, deployment and scale.

The ideal candidate is someone who can move comfortably between a user conversation in the field, a product requirement with an engineering team, a roadmap discussion with leadership and a deployment conversation with a government stakeholder.

Key Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Discovery

Own the product lifecycle from problem discovery to deployment and continuous improvement.
Work with users, government stakeholders and domain experts to identify problems and translate them into product opportunities.
Conduct user interviews, field visits, workshops and discovery exercises to understand workflows, pain points and unmet needs.
Define product vision, objectives, user personas, journeys and key use cases.

Product Analytics & Improvement

Establish feedback loops between users, implementation teams and product development.
Monitor product performance after deployment and drive continuous improvement.
Stakeholder & Implementation Management

Manage expectations across stakeholders while maintaining a clear product direction.
Support product pilots, demonstrations, training and adoption activities.
Travel across Andhra Pradesh to understand implementation realities and work directly with users.
What We Are Looking For

4–8 years of experience in product management, preferably in technology products, SaaS, digital platforms, data products or AI-enabled products.
Strong understanding of the end-to-end product management lifecycle.
Experience working with engineering and design teams to build and launch digital products.
Strong ability to convert ambiguous problems into clearly defined product requirements and priorities.
Experience with PRDs, user stories, product roadmaps, backlog management, prioritisation and product analytics.
Good technical understanding of APIs, databases, integrations, data and modern software systems.
Strong analytical and problem-solving ability.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
Fluent in Telugu and English, both written and spoken.
Willingness to be based in Vijayawada and travel regularly across Andhra Pradesh.
Good to have

Experience in one or more of the following would be valuable:

Government or public-sector technology products
Agriculture, horticulture, livestock or fisheries
Rural technology or digital public infrastructure
AI or data products
SaaS or enterprise software
Digital transformation programmes
Field-based technology deployments
Working with state government departments or large institutional stakeholders
Domain experience is not mandatory. We are equally interested in strong product managers who have demonstrated the ability to learn complex domains quickly and work effectively with domain experts.

The kind of person we are looking for

You should be comfortable asking “What problem are we actually solving?” before asking what technology we should build.

You should enjoy spending time with users, understanding how work happens on the ground, challenging assumptions and then working with technical teams to turn those insights into products.

You should also be comfortable with the realities of product development: making trade-offs, prioritising limited engineering capacity, managing dependencies, dealing with imperfect requirements and continuously improving a product after it goes live.

Most importantly, you should be interested in building technology that is actually used and creates measurable value, rather than technology for its own sake.

Why this role

This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of technology, AI, government and real-world implementation, with the opportunity to shape products that can operate at scale across Andhra Pradesh.

You will work across multiple domains including Agriculture, Horticulture, Livestock and Fisheries, giving you exposure to complex operational problems and the opportunity to build products that directly interact with large public programmes and field ecosystems.

We are specifically looking for a Product Manager with proven, hands-on experience in owning and building B2B SaaS / technology products.

The ideal candidate should have experience across 0-to-1 and 1-to-N product journeys—from identifying problems and validating opportunities to defining, building, launching, scaling, and continuously improving products.

About the Company

The company provides a customizable suite of advanced tools designed to streamline processes, ensure compliance, and improve product quality, empowering organizations of all sizes.

Role Overview

You will work closely with the CEO, engineering, design, QA, marketing, sales, and functional teams to identify customer problems, define product opportunities, build new products from 0-to-1, and evolve existing products from 1-to-N.

Key Responsibilities

Work closely with sales, marketing, and functional consulting teams on product positioning, customer requirements, and go-to-market initiatives.
Engage directly with customers and stakeholders to understand problems, validate solutions, and gather product insights.
Maintain Jira or other product/project management platforms to support the technology team and ensure execution visibility.

Required Skillset

Description

As part of the AWS Applied AI Solutions organization, we have a vision to provide business applications, leveraging Amazon’s unique experience and expertise, that are used by millions of companies worldwide to manage day-to-day operations. Are you interested in re-inventing the physical store Experience? Just Walk Out (JWO) enables shopping in retail stores with no lines and no checkout. You simply use a credit card to enter the store, take what you want from our selection of fresh, delicious meals and grab and go essentials, and leave the store. This checkout-free shopping experience is made possible by the Just Walk Out (JWO) Technology, which automatically detects whether products are taken or returned, and enables shoppers to grab and go from stores ranging from stadiums, small airport kiosks to massive university stores.

The Senior Product Manager will be responsible for working with software, design, operations, and other teams to expand the magic of JWO technology to a wide array of new selection offered in Amazon's physical stores. You will need to be equally at home understanding and championing the needs of your customers as you are with diving deep on the technology and operational implications of the products you build. You must have a strong track record of successfully launching products.

You exhibit high proficiency and efficacy in core product management disciplines such as defining user stories, priorities, success metrics, presenting vision that works backwards from customers, and are comfortable driving clarity across multiple stakeholders in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment. A successful candidate will combine an ability to Think Big with keen attention to detail. Our team puts a high value on work-life balance. It isn’t about how many hours you spend at home or at work; it’s about the flow you establish that brings energy to both parts of your life. We believe striking the right balance between your personal and professional life is critical to life-long happiness and fulfillment. We offer flexibility in working hours and encourage you to find your own balance between your work and personal lives.

Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. QAD is a leading provider of ERP solutions purpose-built for manufacturing industries — automotive, life sciences, food & beverage, high tech, and industrial. QAD's AI Platform is the domain intelligence layer that sits between the ERP and autonomous AI agents. Job Description

This role owns the full product lifecycle for QAD's Copilot, Search, and Conversational Analytics capabilities — from architecture through to market launch. You will define what gets built, why it matters to manufacturing users, and how it reaches them: shaping the product vision, driving engineering delivery, and partnering with GTM to ensure adoption.

The intelligence that powers these surfaces — how queries are understood, how manufacturing context is assembled, how data is retrieved, and how responses are generated — is where QAD's AI moat is built. You will need to engage deeply with these layers, not as an engineer but as the product owner who defines the contracts, quality standards, and sequencing decisions that determine whether they work in production at enterprise scale.

You will report to the Head of Platform Product, with day-to-day direction from the Director of the AI Platform org. This role is evaluated through the quality of your product thinking, your influence on engineering direction, and the outcomes you drive in the market.

The Opportunity

Manufacturing users today cannot query their own operations without analysts, BI tools, or pre-built reports. QAD's AI platform changes this — but only if the Copilot and Search layer is built correctly and lands with users. You will own both sides of that equation.

Define the semantic search and conversational analytics product that allows manufacturing users to query operational data — orders, inventory, suppliers, quality records — in natural language, without SQL or BI expertise
Own the intelligence contract: how queries are understood, how manufacturing context is assembled, how retrieval is orchestrated, and how responses are grounded in governed data — the foundational decisions that determine product quality at scale

Drive the conversational analytics strategy: how natural language queries translate into analytical results across manufacturing data domains without exposing SQL or BI complexity to the user
Specify the disambiguation model: how the Copilot handles ambiguous queries, missing context, and conflicting data signals in real manufacturing workflows

Search

Own the product definition for QAD's semantic search layer: indexing strategy, query understanding, entity recognition, ranking, and result structure across manufacturing data domains
Define the search intent taxonomy — operational (find order, trace shipment), analytical (show trends, compare periods), and diagnostic (why is this delayed, what caused this variance) — and specify result formats by intent type
Drive the federated search architecture: how results from ERP operational data, analytical stores, and the knowledge graph are ranked and merged into a coherent, useful response

Discovery, Delivery & GTM

Maintain a structured customer discovery programme — extracting real manufacturing query patterns and translating findings into specific product and architecture implications
Own the product backlog: writing stories to Staff Engineer level of specificity — API contracts, state machines, data flows, edge cases — that engineering can build without verbal clarification
Partner with GTM to define the launch and adoption strategy for Copilot and Search: positioning, sales enablement, onboarding playbooks, and the narrative that lands with manufacturing buyers
Define the quality framework for these surfaces: what signals matter for product performance — retrieval relevance, grounding rate, latency distribution — and how they inform roadmap decisions

Stakeholder Management & Managing Up

Proactively surface dependencies, risks, and scope changes to the Director and Head of Platform Product — with a resolution proposal, not just an escalation
Communicate product and architecture decisions clearly to non-technical stakeholders — translating trade-offs into business implications without jargon
Build credibility with Engineering, Architecture, and GTM through the quality and precision of written work

Qualifications

Product Experience

7–12 years in product management, with significant time owning AI-powered, search, or analytics products in enterprise B2B environments — from definition through production launch
Proven track record owning the full product lifecycle: customer discovery, specification, engineering delivery, and GTM — not just one slice
Experience working in matrixed organisations — driving outcomes across Platform, Engineering, Architecture, and GTM without direct authority
Evidence of structured discovery practice applied to a technical product surface — ability to extract product implications from user research, not just UX insights

Core Technical Depth — Required

These are the primary technical domains this role owns. Strong command is expected from day one.

Semantic search architecture: indexing strategy, query understanding, entity recognition, ranking models, and relevance evaluation at enterprise scale
Conversational AI product design: how natural language queries are translated into structured analytical results across complex, domain-specific data without exposing backend complexity to users
LLM-integrated product specification: grounding strategies, hallucination mitigation, response quality gates, and context window management — sufficient to define product contracts engineering builds against
Data platform fluency: OLAP vs operational DB reads, federated search across heterogeneous stores, and how data freshness constraints affect product quality — sufficient to hold authoritative conversations with data engineers
SQL and data modelling: sufficient to validate query plans, understand schema implications, and reason through retrieval architecture trade-offs

Working Familiarity — Expected to Grow Into

These domains sit in adjacent platform layers that Copilot and Search consume. Deep expertise is not required on day one, but working fluency is expected — and will expand as the platform scales toward agentic capabilities.

Intent detection and query understanding pipelines: how user inputs are parsed, classified, and routed across platform layers
Context assembly and packaging: how metric definitions, entity relationships, and business

AI and Agentic Platform

Own platform capabilities including agent orchestration, model and tool integration, context and knowledge management, evaluation frameworks, observability, governance, and reusable agent infrastructure.

6-8+ years of Product Management experience, including 1-2 years of hands-on experience leading technically complex agentic platforms and building AI agents in production, and experience in data visualization, analytics, or business intelligence.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical teams, customers, and senior leadership.

Experience building enterprise AI products where reliability, governance, privacy, security, and explainability are critical.
Familiarity with agent interoperability standards and architectures, such as MCP, agent-to-agent communication, structured tool calling, and multi-agent systems.

PubMatic is one of the world’s leading scaled digital advertising platforms, offering more transparent advertising solutions to publishers, media buyers, commerce companies and data owners, allowing them to harness the power and potential of the open internet to drive better business outcomes.

About the Role
Delhivery moves millions of shipments a day across one of the most complex physical networks: pickups, line-haul, sorting, last-mile, returns, and cross-border. Every one of those steps generates data, decisions, and money on the table. We believe the next decade of logistics will be won by whoever applies AI most intelligently to the physical world.
We are building a team of Product Managers who will reimagine logistics with an Agentic first approach. You won't be bolting a chatbot on a dashboard. You will own problems where a better model or a smarter agent changes unit economics, customer experience, or network reliability at national scale.
.What You’ll Do
Find the right problems. Spend time in hubs, with riders, ops leaders, and merchants. Translate messy operational pain into opportunities for creating a seamless flow that scales.
Own outcomes, not outputs. Define success metrics tied to cost per shipment, delivery success, NPS, or revenue, and be accountable for moving them.
Ship AI products that real operators use. Design human-in-the-loop workflows, fallbacks, and feedback loops so models earn trust on the ground and keep improving after launch.
Drive adoption across the org. Work with Operations, Sales, Finance, and Customer Experience to embed AI into how teams actually work.
Partner deeply with data science and engineering. Shape problem formulation, data requirements, evaluation methodology, and model-versus-rules trade-offs. Understand precision/recall, drift, latency, and cost well enough to challenge and be challenged.
Run rigorous experimentation. A/B tests, shadow deployments, and phased rollouts across geographies and hubs, with clear go/no-go criteria.
Stay at the frontier. Evaluate new LLM, agentic, and vision capabilities, and decide pragmatically what to build, buy, or fine-tune.
The kind of problems you could own
Network intelligence: demand forecasting, capacity planning, dynamic routing, and ETA prediction across the network
Last-mile optimization: address intelligence and geocoding, delivery-attempt prediction, route and slot optimization, rider productivity
Computer vision on the ground: shipment damage detection, automated weighing and dimensioning, sort-center throughput, proof-of-delivery verification
Generative AI and agents: autonomous customer support, ops copilots for hub managers, document and invoice automation, internal knowledge assistants
Risk and trust: fraud, RTO (return-to-origin) prediction, NDR resolution, and merchant risk scoring
Pricing and commercial intelligence: dynamic pricing, serviceability, and yield optimization
You will be matched to problem statements based on impact, your strengths, and the stage of each problem. Expect to work across more than one.

What We’re Looking For
Experience
2–5 years in product management, ideally with at least 1–2 years shipping ML or AI-driven products (or a strong data science, ML engineering, or analytics background that you have transitioned into product)
A track record of taking a product from ambiguous problem to measurable business impact
Strong academic grounding; engineering degree from a top-tier institution preferred, MBA a plus but not required
Skills
Working fluency in ML concepts: model evaluation, training data quality, feedback loops, and the practical differences between classical ML, deep learning, and LLM-based systems
Hands-on comfort with data: SQL is a must, Python or notebooks a plus. You pull your own numbers.
Experience with, or sharp point of view on, GenAI product design: prompt and eval design, RAG, agents, guardrails, and cost/latency trade-offs
Excellent structured thinking and the ability to communicate with engineers, data scientists, and frontline ops leaders equally well
Bias to action, ownership, and comfort operating in complex, high-volume, real-world environments
Pedigree signals we value
Prior experience at product-led or AI-forward companies (marketplaces, e-commerce, mobility, fintech, SaaS, or AI-native startups)
Evidence of impact: shipped models or AI features with quantifiable results, side projects, or published work
Curiosity about the physical world: supply chains, operations, and hardware-meets-software problems

Overview

Role: Product Manager II

Help millions of people discover why Copilot is worth paying for.

Copilot is becoming the AI companion people reach for at work, and more and more of those moments happen on a phone. Every day, people discover something new Copilot can do for them. Your job is to make sure that, when they are ready for more, the path to a paid plan is clear, helpful and genuinely valuable. You will own real experiments on a product used around the world, learn fast and see your work land with customers in weeks, not years.

Why this role, why now

Copilot recently came together as one app across web, desktop and mobile, with chat, agents and creation in a single experience. Monetization is moving inside the product, where value is felt. Early signals on mobile are strong, and in-app purchase is now live on iOS and Android. It is an exciting moment to join: the patterns for monetizing AI are being invented now.

How we work

Small, empowered mission teams with clear ownership.
Every bet starts with a written hypothesis, is measured rigorously, and decisions are made on evidence.
AI-native by default: we use AI agents and tools throughout our own workflow to research, prototype, analyze and ship faster.
Ship fast, learn faster, scale what works.
India shapes global strategy here, not just execution.

You'll thrive here if…

You would rather own the outcome, good or bad, than be shielded from it.
You love turning data and customer insight into a sharp idea worth testing.
You form a view, test it quickly and update it when the data disagrees.
You thrive with high ownership and ask for help early.
You already use AI to work faster and keep exploring what else it can do.
Shipping often sounds energizing, not exhausting.

This role may not be for you if…

You want a fully specified plan handed to you every quarter.
You prefer long studies to running a test and learning from it.
You measure success by features launched rather than customers who find value.

Why join us

This is a chance to shape how AI is experienced and valued by people around the world, early in your career and at real scale. You will learn alongside a fast-moving, AI-native team, own outcomes from day one and grow quickly. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, we would love to meet you.

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

What you will own

At this level you own a well-scoped mission end to end and the metric that goes with it, and you grow quickly toward larger scope.

Upgrade moments: value-led upgrade experiences across Copilot and Microsoft 365 apps on mobile.
The path to paid: experiences that help people and their organizations move to paid plans with confidence.
An experiment portfolio: write the hypothesis, design the test, specify the telemetry, ship with engineering and design, read out the result and decide.
A metric that is yours: such as engagement with upgrade experiences or paid conversion, and a clear story of what moved it.

Your first 30 / 60 / 90 days

First 30 days: learn the product, customers and data deeply.
By 60 days: ship your first hypothesis-led experiment from a crisp spec engineers love.
By 90 days: run several experiments at once and own a metric you can move.

OR equivalent experience.

About The Role

The SBU Connectivity Product Management Lead is the portfolio-level owner for product management, product evolution, go-to-market orchestration, and lifecycle value realization across SBU Connectivity. The role consolidates the former product-specific Business Lead responsibilities into one Product Management organization while maintaining distinct product lines for telematics and connectivity offerings and clear interfaces with the Global Business Lead for overall commercial/business ownership.

You will translate market, customer, technology, and RFQ signals into a coherent portfolio roadmap, investment priorities, differentiated product propositions, and executable business cases. Drive a product-first operating model that increases reuse, reduces bespoke development, improves R&D return, and strengthens global market adoption through close partnership with NPI, Systems/Solution Architecture, Product Engineering, Global RFQ/Early Engagement, Global Delivery, Finance, Sales, and the Global Business Lead.

You will lead a globally distributed team of product managers and regional GTM product managers and influences a broad matrix spanning engineering, architecture, delivery, finance, sales, marketing, and customer teams. Success requires enterprise-level judgment across multiple product lines, regions, customers, investment horizons, and technology generations.

Manage the global Product Management organization spanning telematics/connectivity product lines and regional GTM product management in the Americas, Europe, Japan, India/APAC and other priority markets. You

will build a strong product management discipline with common methods for roadmaps, business cases, product requirements, lifecycle governance, GTM readiness and portfolio decision making.

What You Will Do

Own Portfolio Product Management: Drive product evolution, 3–5-year roadmaps and lifecycle decisions across Connectivity, balancing customer value, technical feasibility, and profitability. 
Lead GTM & Regional Product Management: Convert market and Voice-of-Customer signals into product priorities, positioning, value propositions, sales enablement and launch readiness. 
Partner for Growth: Work with Global Business Lead, Sales and RFQ/Early Engagement to shape opportunities around scalable products and derivatives rather than bespoke solutions. 
Own Product Business Cases & Value Realization: Establish product investment logic across market potential, pricing, revenue, margin, R&D, lifecycle cost, reuse and ROI in partnership with Finance. 
Manage Product Performance: Track adoption, pipeline fit, reuse, financial contribution, roadmap execution and customer feedback, taking corrective action when expected value is not realized. 
Connect NPI to Product Ownership: Partner with NPI to mature new concepts and technology opportunities into validated product propositions with disciplined transition into portfolio ownership. 
Drive Cross-Functional Product Realization: Partner with Architecture, Engineering and Global Delivery to translate market needs into scalable platforms, executable roadmaps and reusable production-ready releases. 
Establish Product Management Excellence: Standardize MRD/PRD, roadmap, business case, launch, lifecycle and decision frameworks while resolving cross-product priorities at portfolio level. 
Build Global Product Leadership: Develop a high-performing global Product Management and GTM organization with strong accountability, a customer-centric, data-driven, product-first culture. 

What You Need To Be Successful

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business or a related field; advanced technical or business degree preferred. 
20+ years of progressive experience in automotive, connectivity, technology or adjacent industries, including significant leadership responsibility across product management, business development, GTM and product commercialization. 
10+ years leading senior, globally distributed teams and complex matrix organizations across multiple regions, customers and product lines. 
Demonstrated ownership of multi-product roadmaps, product lifecycle decisions, business cases, pricing/value propositions, investment prioritization and go-to-market execution. 
Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to balance revenue, margin, R&D investment, product reuse, time-to-market and long-term portfolio value. 
Broad understanding of automotive connectivity and telematics technologies including cellular/5G, V2X, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/GNSS, cloud/edge services, cybersecurity, OTA and automotive-grade hardware/software platforms. 
Proven ability to convert customer and market needs into differentiated, scalable product propositions while resisting unnecessary bespoke complexity. 
Executive communication and influencing skills with credibility across customers, senior leadership, engineering, sales, finance, partners and globally distributed teams. 
Ability to make high-quality decisions under ambiguity and lead transformation across organizational boundaries without relying solely on direct authority. 

Bonus Points if You Have

MBA or advanced degree paired with a technical undergraduate degree. 
Experience leading telematics/connectivity portfolios spanning mobility segments. 
Experience with ecosystem partnerships, new business models, software/services monetization and global OEM commercialization. 

What Makes You Eligible

You are willing to travel up to 30% domestic and 15% international travel. 
Due to the nature of global teams and customer base, you understand that flexibility in working hours is required. 

What We Offer

Flexible work environment, allowing for full-time remote work globally for positions that can be performed outside a HARMAN or customer location. 
Access to employee discounts on world-class Harman and Samsung products (JBL, HARMAN Kardon, AKG, etc.). 
Extensive training opportunities through our own HARMAN University. 
Competitive wellness benefits. 
Tuition reimbursement. 
“Be Brilliant” employee recognition and rewards program. 
An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development. 

You Belong Here

HARMAN is committed to making every employee feel welcomed, valued, and empowered. No matter what role you play, we encourage you to share your ideas, voice your distinct perspective, and bring your whole self with you – all within a support-minded culture that celebrates what makes each of us unique. We also recognize that learning is a lifelong pursuit and want you to flourish. We proudly offer added opportunities for training, development, and continuing education, further empowering you to live the career you want.

Ever since the 1920s, we’ve been amplifying the sense of sound. Today, that legacy endures, with integrated technology platforms that make the world smarter, safer, and more connected.

Across automotive, lifestyle, and digital transformation solutions, we create innovative technologies that turn ordinary moments into extraordinary experiences. About Us

HEAD OF PRODUCT BUSINESS UNIT

Anchanto | Pune, India | Reports to the Chief Executive Officer | Unit of 12 to 45 people

About Anchanto

Anchanto is an e-commerce and supply chain technology company headquartered in Singapore, with offices in twelve countries across Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Europe and its largest engineering center in Pune. Brands, retailers and logistics service providers use our purpose built SaaS products to run and scale their e-commerce and omnichannel operations: Order Management, Warehouse Management, Anchanto Grid with more than 200 ready integrations to marketplaces, carriers and enterprise systems, Parcel Tracking, Control Tower and Operations Experience, with Vantage AI as the data and insights layer across all of them. Our AI enabled agentic services, launching soon, help customers run their commerce operations with less manual work and faster decisions. More than 360 enterprise customers, including L'OrÃ©al, Panasonic, EstÃ©e Lauder, DKSH, Toll and Bosch, process over 200 million orders a year through Anchanto across more than 700 warehouses. Anchanto is an Asendia portfolio company.

THE ROLE

A Product Business Unit (PBU) is Product Management and Engineering for one product, brought together as a single threaded organization with one head, one backlog and one set of priorities. The head owns the product's market position, strategy, roadmap, engineering, quality, reliability and business results, and leads the engineers who build it. This is how the leading software companies are organized today: Amazon's single threaded leaders and two pizza teams, the autonomous product units at Spotify and Atlassian, the product clouds at Salesforce and Adobe each run as a business. It removes the handoffs, competing priorities and diffused accountability of separate product and engineering functions, and puts one leader in charge who decides and answers for the result.

This is not a pure product management role. You lead the engineering team as well as the product team, you own the technical quality of what ships, and you are measured on outcomes, not activities. It is the role of building a product business that leads its category: you set where the product goes, build it with your own engineering team, put it in front of the market with the revenue teams, and answer for what it earns and how customers experience it.

WHAT YOU OWN: PRODUCT STRATEGY, ROADMAP, ENGINEERING, DECISIONS AND RESULTS

Product strategy. You know your market and competitors better than anyone in the company, set the product strategy and the positioning ambition with the industry research leaders, keep the product's gaps against the Gartner, Forrester and IDC criteria on your roadmap with dates, and give the CROs your input on pricing and packaging. 
Roadmap and priorities. One backlog covering the roadmap, customer commitments, innovation and tech debt, with the trade offs made by you within the portfolio allocation the CEO sets. Customer priorities and asks come to you from the Delivery team, your internal customer; you deliver against them and do not overwrite them. 
Decisions. What gets built, in what order and how; technical design within the architecture and security standards the CTO sets; release decisions; and whether your product can meet a scope and a date. No scope or date is committed on your product without your confirmation, and once committed you deliver it. 
The way we build. Specs based, AI assisted engineering is the standard way of working in every unit. You own the spec standard for your product and the readiness gate that stops work starting before decisions, credentials and test windows are in place. Quality is owned by the people who build. 
Results. Product P&L, growth, margin and contribution; reliability, incident response and customer satisfaction for your product; and the people: unit structure, hiring, promotions and a standing innovation and AI sub pod that explores adjacent capabilities. 
Ecosystem. Alignment with the other PBUs on the shared roadmap, the blueprint and joint commitments, and working in step with Product Marketing. 

COMMERCIAL INVOLVEMENT

This is not a sales role and carries no quota. The CROs set market priorities, the go to market and what and how your product is sold; the revenue teams (existing customers, Global Strategic Accounts, Key Account Management) own the customer connect. You help them sell: you step into strategic, complex or at risk deals when asked, and you are the final word on what your product can commit to and when. You do not override or bypass them to reach customers directly.

How You Manage Your People

Every person in the unit has written objectives and two or three KPIs for the quarter, reviewed monthly; nobody is without them thirty days after joining. 
Feedback is direct, factual and given within the week, in writing when it matters. 
You represent the company to your team, not the team to the company. Management debt, wrong decisions, undelivered feedback and unaddressed interpersonal issues, is fixed within thirty days of knowing about it. 
Performance is measured against objectives, not effort or tenure. An underperformer gets a written plan and a date; if it passes you take the decision yourself, including exit. Interns are confirmed and people are promoted only after a documented assessment and a direct conversation. 
The unit reports in numbers, weekly in writing and monthly in the outcome review. 
You talk to your N-1, your N-2 and every individual contributor, with skip level one to ones at least quarterly; you do the final interview of every person joining the unit; and the unit runs on a written meeting cadence you publish in your first thirty days and keep. 

OWNING CUSTOMER ESCALATIONS

An escalation on your product is yours from the moment it is raised until the customer confirms it is closed. You do not trivialize it, and you do not expect the CEO or the CROs to lead it. You own the fix and the communication: first written update within the hour, a fixed written cadence until closed, root cause and corrective action within five working days after. You put proactive monitoring in place so the unit knows before the customer does.

Who Decides What

Decision: Roadmap, prioritization, trade offs, what gets built and how, technical design within architecture guardrails, release decisions within standards.

Decides: You 

Decision: Whether your product can meet a scope and a date; unit structure, hiring and promotions within policy; spend within the approved budget.

Decides: You 

Decision: Customer priority, customer asks, revenue delivery and the external customer commitment and timeline.

Decides: Delivery, with your confirmation on scope and date 

Decision: Pricing and packaging; market priorities; go to market; what and how your product is sold; customer connect.

Decides: CROs and revenue teams, with your input on pricing 

Decision: Portfolio allocation, the blueprint, headcount and total investment, cross PBU priority collisions.

Decides: CEO 

Decision: Technology standards, security and compliance, architecture guardrails, CICD, infrastructure, data and AI platform.

Decides: CTO 

How You Are Measured

You own outcomes, not activities. Story points, releases and features shipped are not on this scorecard. You are judged on the outputs below, and you run the unit on five to eight controllable input metrics that you propose, prove move the outputs, and review every week. Numbers are baselined in your first month and verified by Finance.

Product led revenue enablement

What we look at: Adoption and usage depth of the modules we sell, share of customers on the current version, deals unblocked or lost on product capability, referenceable customers, time to go live 

Retention and unit margin

What we look at: Net revenue retention for your product, churn and its reasons, and the unit's contribution margin after people, infrastructure and del

Dreaming big is in our DNA. It’s who we are as a company. It’s our culture. It’s our heritage. And more than ever, it’s our future. A future where we’re always looking forward. Always serving up new ways to meet life’s moments. A future where we keep dreaming bigger. We look for people with passion, talent, and curiosity, and provide them with the teammates, resources and opportunities to unleash their full potential. The power we create together – when we combine your strengths with ours – is unstoppable. Are you ready to join a team that dreams as big as you do?

Senior Product Manager
Zuddl is the unified event platform that B2B marketing teams at companies like CrowdStrike, Figma, Stripe, TikTok, Checkpoint, and Iterable use to run their most important conferences, field events, and webinars, all from one system. Were backed by Y Combinator, Alpha Wave, and Qualcomm Ventures, and were going after every legacy player in a market thats being rebuilt from scratch.
About the Role
Were looking for a Senior Product Manager who has owned a product end to end before, ideally as a founder, and who works largely on their own.
Youll own a major domain of the Zuddl platform that spans several modules. Examples are the full event workflow from registration through production and check-in, or the data and integration layer that connects events to a customers CRM and marketing stack. You own the roadmap, the technical direction with engineering, and the outcomes for that domain. Leadership will challenge your thinking and add context when you ask for it, but wont set direction for you. You are expected to frame ambiguous problems, make hard tradeoffs, and drive complex cross-functional work without much intervention.
You should also be truly AI-native. At Zuddl, product work runs on AI: research, specs, data analysis, and prototypes that go from problem to something clickable in days. This is how you already work, and you think about where AI creates leverage in the product itself.
What Youll Own Working with people
  • Be the primary driver for complex, high-impact initiatives that cut across modules
  • Lead cross-functional work across engineering, design, PMM, CS, Support, and Sales. Resolve disagreements and keep everyone aligned through ambiguity
  • Make difficult decisions under ambiguity, with strong independent product judgment
Building the roadmap
  • Form your own view of where Zuddl wins, loses, and should differentiate. Spot market changes that should change direction
  • Look past individual requests to find the systemic problems underneath, and decide which gaps deserve real investment
  • Understand not just what competitors built, but why, and where theyre heading. Decide where we match, differentiate, or ignore
  • Prioritize major investments on your own and make the hard tradeoffs
  • Own your OKRs and the roadmap behind them, including how modules fit together as one platform
Building the feature
  • Bring strong customer intuition from repeated exposure to users and workflows. Form a sharp initial view, then use research to validate or challenge it
  • Frame complex, ambiguous problems well. Challenge the premise and reframe before the team commits to a solution
  • Write PRDs with clear justification for every call
  • Have strong judgment on where to match the market, where to differentiate, and where not to invest
  • Find the abstractions and platform investments that unlock multiple future features, without over-generalizing
  • Break complex initiatives into stages that reduce product, customer, and technical risk
  • Say no to low-leverage work, even under customer or internal pressure
  • Hold a very high bar for end-to-end workflows. Catch the subtle friction and inconsistency others miss
  • See second- and third-order consequences before they become customer or engineering problems
Shipping the feature
  • Own the release plan for complex or high-risk launches: feature flags, rollout cohorts, backwards compatibility, and first-time user experience
  • Anticipate what Sales, CS, Support, and Implementation will need, and drive enablement
  • Shape positioning for complex or strategic launches, grounded in customer, market, and competitive understanding
  • Work out why a launch is or isnt working, and decide the right response: product, UX, GTM, or enablement
  • Assess partnership and integration opportunities with external third parties
What Were Looking For
  • 5+ years of product management experience, with a track record of owning a product end to end, from roadmap to execution
  • Founder or founder-like experience strongly preferred: youve built and owned a product with that level of ownership and speed
  • B2B SaaS experience is a must
  • Startup experience is required. Youre comfortable with ambiguity, limited resources, and fast iteration
  • Experience at a marketing- or design-led company is a strong plus. So is event tech or martech
  • Truly AI-native: AI is your default for research, specs, data analysis, and prototyping, and you can show us how
  • You love technology and can hold detailed conversations with your engineering team. An engineering background is a bonus
  • You go deep on data and turn it into decisions
  • Excellent communicator and stakeholder manager. You tell the story well, listen to other views, and still drive the decision thats best for the customer and the business
  • Equally comfortable on the long-term vision, next weeks release, and what went wrong with last months launch
How You Operate
  • High agency: you turn business goals into execution plans without detailed direction
  • First-principles thinker, willing to challenge "how weve always done it"
  • Bias to action: you ship and iterate instead of waiting for perfect information
  • You surface risks early
  • Accountable: you own the wins and the misses
What Success Looks Like
  • Your domain has a clear roadmap the company trusts and a track record of shipping against it
  • Launches land well with customers, and Sales, CS, and Support are ready for them
  • Your decisions hold up, and the team needs little leadership intervention to move
Why You Want To Work Here
  • Competitive compensation
  • ESOPs
  • Remote working, with an option to rent coworking spaces
  • Flexible leave program
  • Home workstation setup allowance
  • A culture built on trust, transparency, and integrity

Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at circle.com.

What You’ll Be Part Of

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. What you'll be responsible for

You will own product areas within Managed Payments, Circle’s regulated payments infrastructure that enables PSPs, financial institutions, banks, and enterprises to use stablecoin-powered payment rails without operating crypto infrastructure themselves. You will define and evolve product capabilities that support managed pay-ins, payouts, conversion, and transaction lifecycle management across stablecoin and fiat endpoints. Working closely with Engineering, Compliance, Operations, Treasury, and commercial teams, you will translate complex customer and business needs into clear product priorities, lead cross-functional execution, and deliver measurable improvements to how customers move money across geographies and payment rails.

What you'll work on

Own the roadmap for product areas across managed pay-ins, payouts, fiat endpoints, conversion, and transaction lifecycle management, aligning priorities with customer needs and Circle’s goals.
Define and launch capabilities that expand Managed Payments across Circle’s regulated hubs, including new entities, corridors, payout methods, and geographic coverage.
Shape simple, reliable customer experiences for accepting funds, converting value, and disbursing globally across stablecoin and fiat rails, including integrations with CPN and other Circle systems.
Improve customer and operator workflows across onboarding, account setup, transaction visibility, reporting, exception handling, reconciliation, refunds, RFIs, and bulk payments.
Use customer, product, payment, and operational data to identify friction, prioritize investments, and measure improvements in reliability, efficiency, adoption, and customer experience.
Evaluate opportunities to support new payment rails, payout use cases, and digital assets based on customer demand, regulatory requirements, technical feasibility, and business priorities.
Lead complex cross-functional initiatives with Engineering, Compliance, Operations, Legal, Treasury, BD, and Product, navigating technical and business trade-offs and driving alignment from definition through launch.

What you'll bring to Circle

Core requirements

4+ years of relevant experience, including product management experience building payments, fintech, financial infrastructure, or similarly complex B2B products.
Experience owning product vision, roadmaps, and execution for B2B capabilities such as payments, pay-ins, payouts, settlement, treasury infrastructure, APIs, or financial operations.
Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex cross-functional initiatives spanning Engineering and partners such as Compliance, Operations, Legal, Treasury, or commercial teams.
Strong analytical and technical fluency, with experience using customer, product, payment, and operational data to identify opportunities and guide product decisions.
Track record of delivering measurable improvements to customer experience, product adoption, operational efficiency, reliability, or business performance.

Why this role matters

What You'll Bring: Qualifications

4+ years of experience in Product Management, specifically within B2B SaaS, Business Intelligence, Data Analytics, or related AI-native platforms. 
Proven track record of successful product delivery and strategic execution in a fast-paced environment. 
Demonstrated technical and data understanding—you must be comfortable discussing APIs, data pipelines, model performance, and architectural trade-offs with customers and engineers. 
Deeply rooted customer empathy and proficiency in interpreting user analytics and business metrics to guide product strategy. 
Strong collaborative and stakeholder management skills across Product, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 

Our CRAFT

CRAFT isn’t a list of aspirational values. It’s how we hire, how we promote, how we resolve hard calls, and how we stay honest with ourselves.

C — Customer trust. Everything starts here. We listen carefully, act with integrity, and respond with urgency. Delight is downstream of trust — never the other way around.

R — Relentless on outcomes. We move with urgency, take initiative, and see things through. Effort isn’t the measure — results are. If something isn’t working, we change the approach now.

A — Authenticity. We say the hard things, directly and with respect. We also show up as full humans. That combination is how trust is earned and how we grow together.

F — First principles, grounded in reality. We don’t accept “that’s how it’s done.” We strip problems to what’s actually true and build up from there — then validate quickly and let real-world results decide.

T — Transparency. We share the why, not just the what. When something can’t be shared, we say so. We’re one team — information flows so we can do our best work and challenge each other when we’re wrong.

We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team where everyone can do their best work.

The Pitch

As Product Owner for Workday HELP, you’ll own how our employees get answers and resolve HR issues: the cases, the knowledge, and the agents that make both smarter. You’ll implement, break things in sandbox, decide what ships, and turn Workday’s newest AI features into something employees actually use. This is a hands-on IC role. You will configure, test, and launch, not manage a backlog from a distance. And the exciting part: you will continue your consulting journey as we roll the implementation to our portfolio companies across the globe. Also, Workday is shipping AI faster than most teams can evaluate it. We want someone who gets excited about that, not overwhelmed by it.

What You’ll Do

Own and implement Workday HELP

Lead end-to-end implementation of Case Management: case categories, case types, routing, SLAs, escalation paths, security, and integrations
Build and run Knowledge Management: article structure, authoring and approval workflows, audience targeting, and content lifecycle
Own the HELP product roadmap, backlog, and release readiness, including triaging each Workday bi-annual release for what matters to us

Experiment With What’s Next

Evaluate and pilot new Workday AI capabilities as they arrive, including Illuminate and self-service agents
Run structured experiments: define the hypothesis, configure in sandbox, test with real scenarios, and measure results
Make clear, evidence-backed recommendations on what to adopt, defer, or skip
Help shape our agent-led self-service approach, from deflection to guided resolution

Make it measurable

Define the metrics for HR service delivery: case volume, resolution time, deflection, knowledge usage, and employee satisfaction
Build case analytics and dashboards that show leaders what is working and where to act next

Work across the Workday ecosystem

Partner with Core HCM, Talent, Recruiting, and Payroll teams so HELP works smoothly with the rest of the platform
Work with People Operations, HR Centers of Excellence, and IT on process design, content ownership, and change management
Coordinate with Workday and implementation partners on features, defects, and early-adopter programs

What You Bring

Must-haves

Hands-on Workday HELP implementation experience. This is non-negotiable. You have taken Case Management and/or Knowledge Management from design to go-live
Strong Core HCM background. You understand worker data, business processes, security, organizations, and how HELP depends on all of it
Experience as a product owner, functional lead, or senior consultant who owns configuration, not just requirements
Ability to translate HR service needs into clear user stories, configuration designs, and test plans
Strong stakeholder communication across HR, IT, and business teams

Strong plus

Experience implementing or piloting Workday self-service agents or Illuminate AI features
Case management analytics experience (Workday reporting, people analytics, or dashboards on case data)

What Makes You a Top Candidate

Experience in Peakon, Learning, or Journeys. We want someone who sees how HELP connects to the wider employee experience, such as a Journey that triggers a case or Peakon feedback that reshapes knowledge content
Workday certifications in HCM or related modules
Prior experience in a shared services or global HR environment

You’ll Thrive Here If You

Treat every new Workday release like a gift basket and open it immediately
Are comfortable saying “that didn’t work, here’s why, here’s what we do instead”
Prefer building and testing over writing 40-page decks
Care about the employee on the other end of the case, not just the configuration
Can make a judgment call with 80% of the information

Why This Role

To bring HELP to life, hands on. 
Early access to evaluating Workday’s AI roadmap, with real influence on what we adopt
A role built around experimentation, not maintenance
Visible impact: every employee touches HELP
Opportunity to grow into broader People Technology and AI-in-HR leadership as our platform scope expands

Why Skan AI

We're in hyper-growth mode at exactly the right moment in history. As enterprises race to adopt agentic AI, we're uniquely positioned to deliver the clear signal they desperately need: a platform that trains and grounds AI Agents in trillions of real execution signals, enabling reliable, compliant automation of their most complex processes.

Backed by Dell Technologies Capital and other leading investors, we're the only company that can bridge the gap between AI's promise and enterprise reality, making us perfectly positioned to define the agentic era for modern enterprises.
